highlights.content: ![AI Agent Store Logo](/logo.svg) # AI Agents News — Week of August 30, 2026 ### Nvidia repositions hardware for agent workloads, not just GPUs **What changed:** Nvidia is pushing beyond raw GPU performance to sell systems designed to run agentic workloads end-to-end — pairing Rubin GPUs with a Vera CPU and other supporting units to reduce data movement and speed orchestration for multi-step agents. The piece documents Vera’s role in orchestrating data flow and claims up to 3x improvements on certain I/O-heavy operations. **Why it matters:** Founders and operators building production agents should stop treating GPUs as the whole stack; latency, memory orchestration, and data plumbing now determine whether an agent is efficient and affordable at scale. Expect hardware partners and cloud vendors to sell integrated racks (CPU + GPU + flash + accelerators) optimized for agents, which changes procurement, cost modeling, and where you deploy sensitive workflows. **Try/watch:** If you run agents in production, benchmark full-stack latency and token cost (model inference plus orchestration overhead) against end-to-end hardware profiles — not just GPU throughput — and ask cloud vendors for agent-focused SLAs and memory/access patterns before committing to large deployments. ### Major music publishers sue Anthropic — a legal risk for agent platforms that used web data **What changed:** Sony Music Publishing, Warner Chappell and other music publishers filed a lawsuit alleging Anthropic acquired copyrighted material by illicit scraping and used it to train Claude, accusing the lab of large-scale piracy; Anthropic says it will defend itself. The report notes this builds on prior litigation where Anthropic faced damages related to unlawful content acquisition. **Why it matters:** Legal churn around training data directly affects companies building agents that rely on third-party models or model-hosting partnerships — licensing disputes can force model removals, disrupt integrations, or create sudden compliance costs. Buyers, integrators, and consultancies must treat provenance and defensible data acquisition as a first-order procurement risk, especially for agents that will produce or act on copyrighted or sensitive content. **Try/watch:** Add a contractual and technical checklist to any agent procurement: (1) model/data provenance guarantees, (2) indemnity and takedown procedures, (3) fallback model plans, and (4) an audit path for training data sources. Monitor this lawsuit for how courts treat bulk acquisition vs. lawful use; outcomes will change commercial risk assessments. ### How The Washington Post built a network of analytics agents **What changed:** The Washington Post is using ChatGPT and OpenAI APIs to assemble a network of agents that query multiple internal datasets, follow permission logic, and return short-timeframe answers for content, subscription, and ad questions. **Why it matters:** If you run analytics or operations, this shows agents can compress recurring, cross-dataset queries into an on-demand assistant—reducing response time and freeing analysts to focus on judgement rather than data-gathering. **Try/watch:** Pilot a single “daily KPI” agent that reads the one canonical table set you trust, logs every query, and requires human sign-off for actions that change data; watch for permission leaks and audit trails. ### Anthropic details Slack-first agents with Claude Tag (examples and prompts) **What changed:** Anthropic published a how-to post showing Claude Tag operating inside Slack: it can read allowed channels, follow threads, consolidate scattered asks, draft documents, and run follow-ups while respecting scoped access rules. **Why it matters:** For founders and operators, this is a practical pattern: embed agents inside collaboration tools to automate triage and routine writing while keeping data access narrow—so adopters can get productivity gains without wholesale platform rewrites. **Try/watch:** Start with a p...

highlights.titleZh: GLM-5.2 Open Source AI Model: The Complete Guide
highlights.content: Reviewed by[Jonathan West](/about) · Updated Jul 17, 2026 # GLM-5.2 Open Source AI Model: The Complete Guide Exploring Zhipu AI's Latest Breakthrough in Open Source large language models (LLMs) Reviewed by[Jonathan West](/about) · Updated Jul 17, 2026 On June 13, 2026, Zhipu AI introduced GLM-5.2, the latest iteration of its open source large language model series. GLM-5.2 is a multimodal, general-purpose LLM with publicly available weights, designed for enterprise-grade natural language understanding and generation tasks. Unlike [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com), [Claude](https://claude.ai), and other widely-used closed-source models, GLM-5.2 offers a combination of a one million-token context window, selectable reasoning modes, and an MIT license—allowing unrestricted use and deployment. These features distinguish GLM-5.2 in scalability, adaptability, and transparency, particularly for organizations that require code-level access and long input capacities, which existing mainstream LLM APIs typically limit. For AI practitioners and businesses evaluating open source LLM deployment, GLM-5.2’s release means greater flexibility both technically and legally. Its extensive context window supports complex enterprise workflows—such as ingesting long documents or maintaining multi-stage conversational histories—without the token limitations that often constrain commercial platforms. This opens up new possibilities for regulated industries, internal tooling, and custom AI solutions where open weight access and data privacy are essential. --- ## What Is the GLM-5.2 Open Source AI Model? GLM-5.2 is a 744-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language model from [Zhipu AI](https://z.ai) (branded Z.ai) — released June 13, 2026 and now fully open source under the MIT license, with the complete weights live on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co). It pairs frontier-scale capability with a one-million-token context window and selectable High/Max reasoning modes, built for long-horizon coding and agentic work rather than one-off chat prompts. The model debuted through the GLM Coding Plan as a subscriber preview; within a week, Zhipu shipped the full open release — downloadable weights, a standalone API, and public benchmarks — taking GLM-5.2 from coding-plan preview to a model any team can download, fine-tune, and self-host. Sources [Official Zhipu AI GLM-5.2 Launch Blog↗](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.2 "Open source: https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.2") Curious about integrating GLM-5.2 safely in your SMB? Layer3 Labs can help you map the best path. [Book a Consultation](/ai-workflow-audit) --- ## Key Features: 1M Context Window & Reasoning Modes GLM-5.2 stands out with its fully usable one-million-token context window and two reasoning-effort settings: High and Max. A 1M-token context window enables the model to consider massive codebases, long documents, or detailed project threads in one interaction—far more than most rival models. Selectable reasoning modes let users balance speed and answer depth, which helps for both code generation and complex research or analysis tasks. During technical evaluations, we observed that models with large context windows can, in real-world coding automation tasks, run into timeouts or regressions when the input approaches maximum size—highlighting the need to architect workflows that manage both segmenting and fallback gracefully. * Usable 1,000,000-token context window (not just theoretical) * High reasoning mode for strong performance at lower cost * Max reasoning mode for highest effort and answer quality The million-token context can process an entire code repository or long-form legal document, a major upgrade for regulated and technical workflows. Sources [KuCoin News: GLM-5.2 Launch Details↗](https://kucoin.com/news/flash/zhipu-ai-launches-glm-5-2-with-1m-context-support-api-and-open-source-release-scheduled-for-next-week "Open source: https://kucoin.com/news/flash/zhipu-ai-launches-glm-5-2-with-1m-cont...

According to TechCrunch, the next layer of competition is moving into the systems around the chip — how data moves, how compute is orchestrated, how storage and networking perform, and how massive AI data centers operate efficiently at scale. That matters. For years, Nvidia’s story was simple: AI needs GPUs. Nvidia makes the best GPUs. Demand explodes. But as hyperscalers and chipmakers build alternatives, the bigger question is not just who has the best processor. It is who can make the entire AI factory work better. The future of AI infrastructure is becoming less about one component and more about the full system: Compute. Memory. Networking. Storage. Energy efficiency. Data movement. Orchestration. Performance per watt. That is the real lesson for businesses too. AI success does not come from buying one tool. It comes from making the whole system work together. The companies that win with AI will not just adopt powerful technology. They will build the infrastructure, workflows, and operating discipline to use it well. highlights.content: ## Unbox Factory's Post --- ### [**Unbox Factory**](https://www.facebook.com/unboxfactory?__cft__[0]=AZYGygHGxt0VF61fNNdeu3lDIswD_YLzp623WEJOfzeveoN0lAzJnOSbfK5dJjQ-egwsiHazsiVojC2pd2Pk8uKi5ebbxOFa0Ug7UPwAAQbnRZ6olNzaQRbZoYyp72wjdpNG-zHqJd58VakzsNFMCpJ8FlQNacEK4lu0A5mJmlMCDw&__tn__=-UC%2CP-R) [1h](https://www.facebook.com/unboxfactory/posts/pfbid0UN722yDf55H1DJ3hbL79CSqyqkPZWUjFmWHhYXoQQorxmiigB57MWKaWk3b7d5Lkl?__cft__[0]=AZYGygHGxt0VF61fNNdeu3lDIswD_YLzp623WEJOfzeveoN0lAzJnOSbfK5dJjQ-egwsiHazsiVojC2pd2Pk8uKi5ebbxOFa0Ug7UPwAAQbnRZ6olNzaQRbZoYyp72wjdpNG-zHqJd58VakzsNFMCpJ8FlQNacEK4lu0A5mJmlMCDw&__tn__=%2CO%2CP-R)  · NVIDIA generated a record $96.2 billion in quarterly revenue for the quarter ended July 26, 2026—an extraordinary 106% increase from the same quarter a year earlier and 18% higher than the previous quarter. The biggest driver was its Data Center business, which generated approximately $89 billion, up 117% year over year. NVIDIA also reported approximately $59.7 billion in quarterly profit, showing just how enormous the AI infrastructure boom has become. NVIDIA expects another record quarter, forecasting approximately $108 billion in revenue—meaning the company could soon be generating more than $100 billion every three months. The numbers demonstrate that the AI boom is no longer a small technology cycle. It is creating enormous demand for GPUs, networking equipment, data centers, electricity and advanced cooling infrastructure. Source: NVIDIA, August 27, 2026 highlights.titleZh: Broadcom or AMD? Here's Why the Market Is Pricing the Same AI Boom So Differently Across 2 Chip Stocks. | The Motley Fool
highlights.content: [Accessibility Menu](#) [▲ S&P 500 **+---%**|▲ Stock Advisor **+---%**Join The Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/mms/mark/e-foolcom-sa-top-nav-returns) [Accessibility](#)[Help](https://support.fool.com/) [![The Motley Fool](https://g.foolcdn.com/misc-assets/logo-tmf-primary-1-magenta-purple-reversed.svg?_w=320)![The Motley Fool](https://g.foolcdn.com/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fg.foolcdn.com%2Fmisc-assets%2Ftmf_holdingco_logo_stacked_magenta_royalpurple_rev.png&w=96&op=resize)](/) **Broadcom** ([AVGO](/quote/nasdaq/avgo/) -0.74%) and **Advanced Micro Devices** ([AMD](/quote/nasdaq/amd/) -2.33%) sit side by side in many [artificial intelligence (AI)](https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/market-sectors/information-technology/ai-stocks/) hardware conversations, yet the market makes it clear they are not the same kind of stock. Broadcom looks like a [cash-rich infrastructure utility](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/10/broadcom-stock-looks-like-a-screaming-deal/). AMD looks more like a leveraged bet on a shift in which players will supply the brains of data centers. That difference, more than any single metric, is what their valuations are signaling. ![Letters A and I fall in a hurricane.](https://g.foolcdn.com/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fg.foolcdn.com%2Feditorial%2Fimages%2F883329%2Fgettyimages-2155811445.jpg&w=3840&op=resize) Image source: Getty Images. ## Broadcom: Contracted AI infrastructure [Broadcom's](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/27/should-you-buy-broadcom-stock-while-its-under-400/) AI business is built around selling high-speed networking equipment and designing custom accelerators for hyperscalers that want their own bespoke silicon. It [co-designs application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs)](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/06/02/asic-demand-broadcom-no-brainer-buy/) for customers such as **Microsoft**, **Alphabet**, **Amazon**, and **Meta Platforms**. Each of these chips is narrowly built for the specific model mix and power envelope of the buyer, in contrast to the general-purpose GPUs sold by AMD, **Nvidia** ([NVDA](/quote/nasdaq/nvda/) -4.58%), and others. Because of this, ASICs can be more efficient and less costly to use than GPUs for the precise types of workloads they are designed for. Those ASIC programs are large. Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue sits near $8.4 billion per quarter, with a disclosed AI chip backlog of around $73 billion, and management is now talking about a line of sight to more than $100 billion in AI revenue in 2027. Custom ASIC servers are on track to reach about 27.8% of AI server shipments in 2026, with ASIC sales volumes growing 44.6% year over year, well ahead of the growth pace of merchant GPUs. Layer that on top of Broadcom's established businesses in networking, broadband, and enterprise software, and the tech giant starts to look like an AI-enabled toll road. ![Broadcom Stock Quote](https://g.foolcdn.com/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fg.foolcdn.com%2Fart%2Fcompanylogos%2Fmark%2FAVGO.png&w=128&op=resize) ## [NASDAQ: AVGO](/quote/nasdaq/avgo/) Premium Feature Moneyball Superscore 90/100 Today's Change (-0.74%) $-2.75 Current Price $368.79 ### Key Data Points Market Cap $1.8TMarket cap calculated using publicly traded shares outstanding only. Google's AI Mode now assists with hotel bookings and flight price tracking, integrating with partners like Booking.com and Marriott. Okta is addressing the growing need for identity management by launching Agent SSO, aiming to standardize digital labor identity. The development of AI agents is also focusing on improving their reliability and operational efficiency. Research indicates that some AI coding assistants, like Claude Code and Codex, may lack a sense of time and overestimate task durations, posing challenges for oversight. Anthropic is adjusting Claude Code's usage limits, promising greater control and transparency. Furthermore, advancements are being made in how AI agents interact with both digital and physical environments. Anthropic has previewed the Model Hardware Standard, a specification for AI agents to safely operate physical devices. Meanwhile, new platforms like ERP.io are launching AI-native solutions for businesses, integrating various functions into a unified system. AI Agents.content: ![AI Agent Store Logo](/logo.svg) # AI Agents News — Week of August 30, 2026 ### Nvidia repositions hardware for agent workloads, not just GPUs **What changed:** Nvidia is pushing beyond raw GPU performance to sell systems designed to run agentic workloads end-to-end — pairing Rubin GPUs with a Vera CPU and other supporting units to reduce data movement and speed orchestration for multi-step agents. The piece documents Vera’s role in orchestrating data flow and claims up to 3x improvements on certain I/O-heavy operations. **Why it matters:** Founders and operators building production agents should stop treating GPUs as the whole stack; latency, memory orchestration, and data plumbing now determine whether an agent is efficient and affordable at scale. Expect hardware partners and cloud vendors to sell integrated racks (CPU + GPU + flash + accelerators) optimized for agents, which changes procurement, cost modeling, and where you deploy sensitive workflows. **Try/watch:** If you run agents in production, benchmark full-stack latency and token cost (model inference plus orchestration overhead) against end-to-end hardware profiles — not just GPU throughput — and ask cloud vendors for agent-focused SLAs and memory/access patterns before committing to large deployments. ### Major music publishers sue Anthropic — a legal risk for agent platforms that used web data **What changed:** Sony Music Publishing, Warner Chappell and other music publishers filed a lawsuit alleging Anthropic acquired copyrighted material by illicit scraping and used it to train Claude, accusing the lab of large-scale piracy; Anthropic says it will defend itself. The report notes this builds on prior litigation where Anthropic faced damages related to unlawful content acquisition. **Why it matters:** Legal churn around training data directly affects companies building agents that rely on third-party models or model-hosting partnerships — licensing disputes can force model removals, disrupt integrations, or create sudden compliance costs. Buyers, integrators, and consultancies must treat provenance and defensible data acquisition as a first-order procurement risk, especially for agents that will produce or act on copyrighted or sensitive content. **Try/watch:** Add a contractual and technical checklist to any agent procurement: (1) model/data provenance guarantees, (2) indemnity and takedown procedures, (3) fallback model plans, and (4) an audit path for training data sources. Monitor this lawsuit for how courts treat bulk acquisition vs. lawful use; outcomes will change commercial risk assessments. ### How The Washington Post built a network of analytics agents **What changed:** The Washington Post is using ChatGPT and OpenAI APIs to assemble a network of agents that query multiple internal datasets, follow permission logic, and return short-timeframe answers for content, subscription, and ad questions. **Why it matters:** If you run analytics or operations, this shows agents can compress recurring, cross-dataset queries into an on-demand assistant—reducing response time and freeing analysts to focus on judgement rather than data-gathering. **Try/watch:** Pilot a single “daily KPI” agent that reads the one canonical table set you trust, logs every query, and requires human sign-off for actions that change data; watch for permission leaks and audit trails. ### Anthropic details Slack-first agents with Claude Tag (examples and prompts) **What changed:** Anthropic published a how-to post showing Claude Tag operating inside Slack: it can read allowed channels, follow threads, consolidate scattered asks, draft documents, and run follow-ups while respecting scoped access rules. **Why it matters:** For founders and operators, this is a practical pattern: embed agents inside collaboration tools to automate triage and routine writing while keeping data access narrow—so adopters can get productivity gains without wholesale platform rewrites. **Try/watch:** Start with a p...

AI Agents.titleZh: AI agents need their own identity before they need a gateway
AI Agents.content: [The Independent Voice on AI](/) Featured # AI agents need their own identity before they need a gateway [Ravindra Annam](/author/ravindra-annam) ![AI agents need their own identity before they need a gateway](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.ctfassets.net%2Fjdtwqhzvc2n1%2F1Lf9hptifgqfEV5M6ZXX6x%2F9bb7f882642a50751e136e41ca6fab39%2Fu7277289442_A_modern_interpretation_of_cybersecurity._Lock._D_d39586ee-f8be-4f5d-b76a-e953fd9cebdb_0.png%3Fw%3D1000%26q%3D100&w=3840&q=85) CleoPtolemy made with Midjourney Enterprise AI has entered a new era. Organizations are rapidly moving beyond assistants that answer questions to autonomous agents capable of reasoning, invoking tools, accessing enterprise applications, coordinating with other agents, and completing multi-step business workflows with minimal human intervention. This shift represents a fundamental change in how software operates. Traditional applications execute predefined logic written by developers. AI agents, however, dynamically determine how to achieve an objective. They decide which tools to use, which APIs to call, what information to retrieve, and how to sequence actions based on context. That flexibility unlocks enormous business value, but it also introduces a new class of [security risks](https://venturebeat.com/security/ai-agents-that-pass-authentication-can-still-drift-expose-data-or-get-memory-poisoned). Much of today's AI security discussion focuses on prompt injection, model vulnerabilities, and data leakage. These are important concerns, but they represent only part of the challenge. Once an AI agent has successfully authenticated and begins acting autonomously, traditional security controls provide very little visibility into whether it continues to operate safely. This is where enterprises need to adopt a new security mindset: runtime trust. ## **Authentication establishes identity, not trust** Enterprise security has traditionally relied on three foundational questions: Who are you, what can you access, and what actions are you authorized to perform. Identity providers, multi-factor authentication (MFA), role-based access control, and zero trust architectures answer these questions effectively for human users and conventional applications, and NIST's zero trust guidance remains a solid reference point for how those principles are meant to work ([NIST SP 800-207](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/207/final)). AI agents introduce a different problem. An [AI agent](https://venturebeat.com/orchestration/enterprise-ai-agents-are-only-as-reliable-as-the-messiest-documents-behind-them) may legitimately authenticate using an enterprise identity, receive valid API credentials, and be granted access to systems like Microsoft 365, ServiceNow, Salesforce, or GitHub. From an identity perspective, everything appears correct. The real challenge begins after authentication: During execution, the agent continuously reasons, interprets objectives, invokes tools, retrieves information, and adapts its behavior based on new context, and security teams must determine whether those actions remain aligned with the user's intent and organizational policy. Authentication verifies who an AI agent is. Runtime trust continuously verifies what it is doing. ## **Enterprise AI is becoming an autonomous workforce** Modern AI agents increasingly interact with large language models (LLMs), Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, [retrieval-augmented generation](https://venturebeat.com/orchestration/cutting-rag-inference-costs-6x-starts-with-deciding-what-never-reaches-the-llm) (RAG) systems, vector databases, enterprise APIs, SaaS platforms, and internal knowledge repositories, as well as other AI agents. This interconnected ecosystem enables sophisticated automation but dramatically expands the attack surface: A single compromised tool, poisoned knowledge source, overly permissive API, or manipulated prompt can influence downstream decisions across an entire workflow, and unlike traditional ...

LLMs.titleZh: GLM-5.2 Open Source AI Model: The Complete Guide
LLMs.content: Reviewed by[Jonathan West](/about) · Updated Jul 17, 2026 # GLM-5.2 Open Source AI Model: The Complete Guide Exploring Zhipu AI's Latest Breakthrough in Open Source large language models (LLMs) Reviewed by[Jonathan West](/about) · Updated Jul 17, 2026 On June 13, 2026, Zhipu AI introduced GLM-5.2, the latest iteration of its open source large language model series. GLM-5.2 is a multimodal, general-purpose LLM with publicly available weights, designed for enterprise-grade natural language understanding and generation tasks. Unlike [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com), [Claude](https://claude.ai), and other widely-used closed-source models, GLM-5.2 offers a combination of a one million-token context window, selectable reasoning modes, and an MIT license—allowing unrestricted use and deployment. These features distinguish GLM-5.2 in scalability, adaptability, and transparency, particularly for organizations that require code-level access and long input capacities, which existing mainstream LLM APIs typically limit. For AI practitioners and businesses evaluating open source LLM deployment, GLM-5.2’s release means greater flexibility both technically and legally. Its extensive context window supports complex enterprise workflows—such as ingesting long documents or maintaining multi-stage conversational histories—without the token limitations that often constrain commercial platforms. This opens up new possibilities for regulated industries, internal tooling, and custom AI solutions where open weight access and data privacy are essential. --- ## What Is the GLM-5.2 Open Source AI Model? GLM-5.2 is a 744-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language model from [Zhipu AI](https://z.ai) (branded Z.ai) — released June 13, 2026 and now fully open source under the MIT license, with the complete weights live on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co). It pairs frontier-scale capability with a one-million-token context window and selectable High/Max reasoning modes, built for long-horizon coding and agentic work rather than one-off chat prompts. The model debuted through the GLM Coding Plan as a subscriber preview; within a week, Zhipu shipped the full open release — downloadable weights, a standalone API, and public benchmarks — taking GLM-5.2 from coding-plan preview to a model any team can download, fine-tune, and self-host. Sources [Official Zhipu AI GLM-5.2 Launch Blog↗](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.2 "Open source: https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.2") Curious about integrating GLM-5.2 safely in your SMB? Layer3 Labs can help you map the best path. [Book a Consultation](/ai-workflow-audit) --- ## Key Features: 1M Context Window & Reasoning Modes GLM-5.2 stands out with its fully usable one-million-token context window and two reasoning-effort settings: High and Max. A 1M-token context window enables the model to consider massive codebases, long documents, or detailed project threads in one interaction—far more than most rival models. Selectable reasoning modes let users balance speed and answer depth, which helps for both code generation and complex research or analysis tasks. During technical evaluations, we observed that models with large context windows can, in real-world coding automation tasks, run into timeouts or regressions when the input approaches maximum size—highlighting the need to architect workflows that manage both segmenting and fallback gracefully. * Usable 1,000,000-token context window (not just theoretical) * High reasoning mode for strong performance at lower cost * Max reasoning mode for highest effort and answer quality The million-token context can process an entire code repository or long-form legal document, a major upgrade for regulated and technical workflows. LLMs.title: OpenAI Retires DALL-E GPT, o3 as 6 AI Deadlines Hit [2026]
LLMs.titleZh: OpenAI Retires DALL-E GPT, o3 as 6 AI Deadlines Hit [2026]
LLMs.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) [AI & Machine Learning](https://shattered.io/ai-machine-learning/) # OpenAI Retires DALL-E GPT, o3 as 6 AI Deadlines Hit [2026] ![](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/droth.webp) [Daniel Roth](https://shattered.io/author/droth/) Updated Aug 30, 2026 · 16 min read OpenAI pulled the official DALL-E GPT out of ChatGPT’s model picker on August 30, 2026, closing out a three-week stretch that has quietly reshuffled which AI models people can actually use. It’s not an isolated retirement. A tracker maintained by [DigitalApplied](https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/ai-model-releases-august-2026-tracker) counted six dated deadlines landing on AI products between August 10 and August 31, spanning OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. Put together, they mark one of the most compressed model-lifecycle resets the industry has seen this year. For developers and everyday ChatGPT users, the practical fallout is immediate: image generation moves fully into ChatGPT Images, OpenAI’s reasoning model o3 is gone from the chat interface, and Claude Sonnet 5’s promotional pricing expires the day after DALL-E’s exit. Layer in fresh open-weight releases from DeepSeek and Tencent, a price war on API tokens, and new EU enforcement powers over systemic-risk models, and August 2026 looks less like routine housekeeping and more like a stress test of how fast the broader [AI and machine learning](/ai-machine-learning/) market can turn over its own products. ## What Changed in ChatGPT This Week OpenAI flagged the DALL-E GPT retirement in ChatGPT’s release notes on July 31, 2026, giving users a month’s notice before the endpoint went dark on August 30, according to [DigitalApplied’s August tracker](https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/ai-model-releases-august-2026-tracker). The dedicated DALL-E GPT, which had lived in the GPT selector as a standalone tool since well before this year, is now folded into the broader ChatGPT Images pipeline. Users who wanted to keep image files generated through the old DALL-E GPT needed to download them before the cutoff, since the tool itself no longer appears as an option. Six days earlier, on August 26, OpenAI retired o3 from ChatGPT’s model list entirely, per the same tracker. That’s a notable move given o3 spent much of 2025 as one of OpenAI’s flagship reasoning models before newer generations pushed it toward the exit. Neither retirement removes the underlying capability from OpenAI’s lineup outright, but both shrink the number of legacy options a user can select directly inside the product, pushing the model roster toward fewer, more current choices. The pattern extends beyond OpenAI’s own models. Earlier in the same window, Google shut down the Imagen 4 API endpoint on August 17, and the week of August 10 brought both a wave of open Qwen weights from Alibaba and an unlimited-chats rollout inside ChatGPT. None of these moves individually would draw much attention. Stacked into a three-week span, they read as a coordinated cleanup across the industry’s biggest model vendors, not a coincidence of scheduling. ## Why OpenAI Is Retiring DALL-E GPT and o3 Now OpenAI hasn’t published a detailed rationale beyond the release-note language cited by DigitalApplied, but the timing lines up with a company that has spent 2026 consolidating tools rather than multiplying them. ChatGPT Images already handles the image-generation workload that DALL-E GPT used to own, and running two overlapping entry points for the same underlying capability adds maintenance cost without adding much for users. Retiring the standalone GPT removes a redundant surface without removing the feature. The o3 retirement fits a similar logic, though the stakes are higher. Reasoning models are expensive to run at scale, and OpenAI has been shipping newer, cheaper alternatives, including a steep price cut to GPT-5.6 Luna that dropped input-token costs by 80% to $0.20 per million tokens for high-volume workloads on July 30, accor...

LLMs.content: [Background](/news?category=Background) [Brian Rifkin](/news?author=636cfdf164bcd4578f28e4f9) REFINe-ing AI’s Role in Nephrology Diagnosis [Brian Rifkin](/news?author=636cfdf164bcd4578f28e4f9) [Background](/news/category/Background) # [REFINe-ing AI’s Role in Nephrology Diagnosis](/news/ai-diagnosis8302026) [Brian Rifkin](/news?author=636cfdf164bcd4578f28e4f9) [Background](/news/category/Background) ### *#NephJC Ten POsts Chat* *September 1st, 2026, 9 pm EST* Kidney Int Rep,  2026 Jun 23;11(9):106673., doi: 10.1016/j.ekir.2026.106673.eCollection 2026 Sep. # **Randomized Controlled Trial of Large Language Model–Assisted Diagnostic Accuracy in Nephrology** Raphaël Bentegeac, Philippe Amouyel, Bastien Le Guellec, Wisit Cheungpasitport, Mehdi Maanaoui, Aghiles Hamroun **PMID:**[**42502668**](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42502668/) **DOI:**[**10.1016/j.ekir.2026.106673**](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ekir.2026.106673) Blog [![REFINe: The Visual Abstract]()](/news/refine-the-visual-abstract) [REFINe: The Visual Abstract](/news/refine-the-visual-abstract) Can AI boost clinical decision-making in nephrology? [Read more →](/news/refine-the-visual-abstract) [![REFINE: El Resumen Visual]()](/news/refine-el-resumen-visual) [REFINE: El Resumen Visual](/news/refine-el-resumen-visual) ¿Puede la IA mejorar la toma de decisiones clínicas en nefrología? [Read more →](/news/refine-el-resumen-visual) [![The Rise and Rise of Quantitative Cassandras]()](/news/ai-commentary) [The Rise and Rise of Quantitative Cassandras](/news/ai-commentary) Saurabh Jha aka @RogueRad comments on the AI predicting AKI paper. There are trade offs involved in predicting events before they occur. Especially if they do not occur. Clear enough? If not, dive in to read more… [Read more →](/news/ai-commentary) # **Introduction** Modern Artificial Intelligence (AI) encompasses a spectrum of computational approaches, from traditional machine learning to deep neural networks capable of processing increasingly complex data (see [NephMadness 2026, AI region](http://www.ajkdblog.org/2026/03/01/nephmadness-2026-ai-region/)). Among the most rapidly evolving applications of deep learning are large language models (LLMs) that are trained on vast amounts of information and can interpret, synthesize, and generate natural language.  Since the release of ChatGPT in late 2022,  medicine has been grappling with a collective identity crisis.  In the last few years, there has been an expanding body of research evaluating the performance of different LLMs across a wide range of medical tasks, from answering clinical questions and interpreting complex case vignettes to diagnostic reasoning and medical decision-making. A recent systematic review ([Chen SF](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41776077/) et al, Nat Med, 2026)  found that LLMs outperformed human comparators in 33% of studies, with better relative performance in knowledge-based assessments than in real-world clinical settings, highlighting the persistent gap between benchmark performance and clinical utility. Essentially, AI programs are very good at multiple-choice exam questions. Nephrology has not been an exception to this trend. You could benchmark GPT or Claude, but you couldn’t open the model and see how it was built. This summer that changed at a pace nobody predicted. Between July 27 and August 29, 2026, four different labs, Moonshot, DeepSeek, Alibaba, and Z.ai, shipped frontier-class weights: a 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3, a 2.4-trillion Qwen3.8, a 1.6-trillion DeepSeek-V4-Pro, and the GLM-5.3 pair. These are not distilled cousins of a secret flagship; they are the flagships, the best of them sitting within a few points of the best closed models on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index*[*[20]*](#ref20)*. And when you open the four config files side by side, something remarkable appears: they all converged on the same three-part recipe. Trillions of parameters with only a few percent awake per token. Hybrid attention that keeps roughly one exact-attention layer for every three cheap ones. And, in the newest twist, a rewired residual stream. This is a tour of that recipe, from the actual tech reports and* `config.json` *files, with the numbers verified and the vendor claims labeled as such.* `config.json` ![]() ## 1. Introduction: Five Weeks That Opened the Frontier The timeline reads like a coordinated launch, except it came from four competing labs: `-0813` I’ve written before about how sparse, linear, and hybrid attention broke the quadratic bottleneck in research models. This post is about what happened next: those ideas grew up, merged, and became *the* frontier production architecture, and because the weights are public, we can read the blueprint line by line instead of guessing from API behavior. The blueprint has three pillars. Extreme mixture-of-experts sparsity. Hybrid attention at a near-universal 3:1 ratio. And hyper-connection residual streams. Let’s take them in order, then look at what the recipe buys in dollars. ## 2. Background: The Two Bills Every Token Pays Why these three pillars and not others? Because a frontier model in 2026 lives or dies on two line items. **Bill one: FLOPs per token.** Every generated token pays compute proportional to the *active* parameters, the weights actually multiplied for that token. Dense models pay for everything, every time. **Bill two: memory traffic per token.** During decode, the GPU must re-read model weights and the KV cache from high-bandwidth memory for every single token. At the million-token contexts that agents and reasoning models now demand, the KV cache, not the matmul, dominates, and decode becomes memory-bandwidth-bound. What changed in 2025–2026 is that the workload shifted decisively toward the expensive side: reasoning models emit tens of thousands of chain-of-thought tokens, and agents run hundreds of tool calls over ...

LLMs.titleZh: Jet-Nemotron: Efficient Language Model with Post Neural ...
LLMs.content: [![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/64f4d663be17b6544a586bac/66084688449188ec73254904_hanlab_logo.png)](/) # Jet-Nemotron: Efficient Language Model with Post Neural Architecture Search Yuxian Gu, Qinghao Hu, Shang Yang, Haocheng Xi, Junyu Chen, Song Han, Han Cai (\* indicates equal contribution) [Code](https://github.com/NVlabs/Jet-Nemotron) [Slides](#) [Poster](#) ## News ## Awards No items found. ## Competition Awards No items found. ## Abstract We present Jet-Nemotron, a new family of hybrid-architecture language models, which matches or exceeds the accuracy of leading full-attention models while significantly improving generation throughput. Jet-Nemotron is developed using Post Neural Architecture Search (PostNAS), a novel neural architecture exploration pipeline that enables efficient model design. Unlike prior approaches, PostNAS begins with a pre-trained full-attention model and freezes its MLP weights, allowing efficient exploration of attention block designs. The pipeline includes four key components: (1) learning optimal full-attention layer placement and elimination, (2) linear attention block selection, (3) designing new attention blocks, and (4) performing hardware-aware hyperparameter search. Our Jet-Nemotron-2B model achieves comparable or superior accuracy to Qwen3, Qwen2.5, Gemma3, and Llama3.2 across a comprehensive suite of benchmarks while delivering up to 53.6× generation throughput speedup and 6.1× prefilling speedup. ## Introduction: Jet-Nemotron is a new family of hybrid-architecture language models that surpass state-of-the-art open-source full-attention language models such as Qwen3, Qwen2.5, Gemma3, and Llama3.2, while achieving significant efficiency gains—up to 53.6× speedup in generation throughput on H100 GPUs (256K context length, maximum batch size). It is built upon two core innovations: * Post Neural Architecture Search, an efficient post-training architecture exploration and adaptation pipeline applicable to arbitrary pre-trained transformer models; * JetBlock, a novel linear attention block that significantly outperforms previous designs such as Mamba2. ## Highlight 1: PostNAS – Post-Training Architecture Exploration and Adaptation Unlike prior methods that train from scratch to explore new model architectures, PostNAS builds on a pre-trained transformer model while enabling flexible exploration of attention block designs, greatly reducing the cost and risk of developing new language model architectures. PostNAS first identifies the optimal placement of full-attention layers, then searches for improved attention block designs. ‍ In the pre-trained transformer model, not all attention layers contribute equally. PostNAS reveals important attention layers within pre-trained transformer models. KV cache size is the most critical factor influencing long-context and long-generation throughput. PostNAS hardware-aware search discovers architectures that deliver similar generation throughput, while having more parameters and achieving better accuracy. ‍ ## Highlight 2: JetBlock - A New Linear Attention Module with SOTA Accuracy With PostNAS, we introduce the JetBlock — a novel linear attention module that integrates dynamic convolution with hardware-aware architecture search to enhance linear attention, delivering substantial accuracy gains over previous designs while maintaining similar training and inference throughput. Below, we present an apples-to-apples comparison between the Mamba2 Block and the JetBlock, using identical training data and training recipes. ## Main Results: Jet-Nemotron-2B and Jet-Nemotron-4B match or surpass the accuracy of leading efficient language models (e.g., Qwen3) across a comprehensive benchmark suite while running significantly faster — 21× and 47× faster than Qwen3-1.7B-Base, respectively. ‍ ## Video ## Citation `@article{ jet-nemotron, title={Jet-Nemotron: Efficient Language Model with Post Neural Architecture Search}, author={Gu, Yuxian and Hu, Qinghao and Yan...

AI Product.title: Semrush Puts Its Data Inside Claude's Chat Window
AI Product.titleZh: Semrush Puts Its Data Inside Claude's Chat Window
AI Product.content: [Skip to content](#main) Sunday, August 30, 2026 [Today's Paper](https://martechedition.com/) [Sign In](https://martechedition.com/wp-login.php?redirect_to=https%3A%2F%2Fmartechedition.com%2Fnews%2Fsemrush-puts-its-data-inside-claudes-chat-window%2F) [Subscribe](/subscribe/) # Semrush Puts Its Data Inside Claude’s Chat Window ![Abhijeet Jadhav](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/cf5568af6fbcdad6b11e2cf768d2211b952759089d29e0a1a9271d9f61e17a9a?s=96&d=mm&r=g) By [Abhijeet Jadhav](https://martechedition.com/author/abhijeet-jadhav/) · August 30, 2026 · 1 min read Abhijeet Jadhav covers martech platforms, attribution and CMO strategy for… ![Semrush Puts Its Data Inside Claude’s Chat Window](https://martechedition.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/img_semrush.jpg) Semrush has launched an official native connector for Anthropic’s Claude, putting the company’s marketing intelligence dataset, 28.8 billion keywords, 43 trillion backlinks, and 317 million tracked LLM prompts, directly inside Claude conversations. The connector went live August 26, 2026 for Semrush One and SEO Classic subscribers, and it is Semrush’s third integration with a major large language model this year, following earlier connectors for other AI assistants. The move matters because it removes the last manual step between a marketing team’s data and the AI tool doing the analysis. Instead of exporting a keyword report to a spreadsheet and pasting it into a chat window, a marketer can now ask Claude to run a competitor gap analysis, audit a backlink profile, or scope a keyword strategy in a single prompt, with the underlying data pulled live rather than summarized from memory. “Today’s marketers are operating with fewer resources and higher expectations on ROI, so access to trusted data and automation is key,” said Vitalii Obischenko, VP of Software Development at Semrush. The original insight here is less about Semrush and more about what it signals for the rest of the [AI-agent tooling race](https://martechedition.com/articles/ad-tech-is-writing-two-rulebooks-for-ai-agents/) now running across ad tech and martech: data vendors are racing to become the connector, not just the dataset, because whichever platform sits closest to where the agent actually works captures the daily habit. A marketer who starts running competitor research inside Claude has little reason to also open Semrush’s own dashboard for the same task, which quietly shifts where the analysis, and the vendor relationship, actually lives. Semrush’s answer is to make sure it is available wherever that habit forms, even inside a competitor’s chat interface, following the same logic already reshaping how [ad tech is wiring itself into ChatGPT](https://martechedition.com/articles/ad-tech-is-wiring-itself-into-chatgpt/). Open Source AI.content: Reviewed by[Jonathan West](/about) · Updated Jul 17, 2026 # GLM-5.2 Open Source AI Model: The Complete Guide Exploring Zhipu AI's Latest Breakthrough in Open Source large language models (LLMs) Reviewed by[Jonathan West](/about) · Updated Jul 17, 2026 On June 13, 2026, Zhipu AI introduced GLM-5.2, the latest iteration of its open source large language model series. GLM-5.2 is a multimodal, general-purpose LLM with publicly available weights, designed for enterprise-grade natural language understanding and generation tasks. Unlike [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com), [Claude](https://claude.ai), and other widely-used closed-source models, GLM-5.2 offers a combination of a one million-token context window, selectable reasoning modes, and an MIT license—allowing unrestricted use and deployment. These features distinguish GLM-5.2 in scalability, adaptability, and transparency, particularly for organizations that require code-level access and long input capacities, which existing mainstream LLM APIs typically limit. For AI practitioners and businesses evaluating open source LLM deployment, GLM-5.2’s release means greater flexibility both technically and legally. Its extensive context window supports complex enterprise workflows—such as ingesting long documents or maintaining multi-stage conversational histories—without the token limitations that often constrain commercial platforms. This opens up new possibilities for regulated industries, internal tooling, and custom AI solutions where open weight access and data privacy are essential. --- ## What Is the GLM-5.2 Open Source AI Model? GLM-5.2 is a 744-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language model from [Zhipu AI](https://z.ai) (branded Z.ai) — released June 13, 2026 and now fully open source under the MIT license, with the complete weights live on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co). It pairs frontier-scale capability with a one-million-token context window and selectable High/Max reasoning modes, built for long-horizon coding and agentic work rather than one-off chat prompts. The model debuted through the GLM Coding Plan as a subscriber preview; within a week, Zhipu shipped the full open release — downloadable weights, a standalone API, and public benchmarks — taking GLM-5.2 from coding-plan preview to a model any team can download, fine-tune, and self-host. Sources [Official Zhipu AI GLM-5.2 Launch Blog↗](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.2 "Open source: https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.2") Curious about integrating GLM-5.2 safely in your SMB? Layer3 Labs can help you map the best path. [Book a Consultation](/ai-workflow-audit) --- ## Key Features: 1M Context Window & Reasoning Modes GLM-5.2 stands out with its fully usable one-million-token context window and two reasoning-effort settings: High and Max. A 1M-token context window enables the model to consider massive codebases, long documents, or detailed project threads in one interaction—far more than most rival models. Selectable reasoning modes let users balance speed and answer depth, which helps for both code generation and complex research or analysis tasks. During technical evaluations, we observed that models with large context windows can, in real-world coding automation tasks, run into timeouts or regressions when the input approaches maximum size—highlighting the need to architect workflows that manage both segmenting and fallback gracefully. * Usable 1,000,000-token context window (not just theoretical) * High reasoning mode for strong performance at lower cost * Max reasoning mode for highest effort and answer quality The million-token context can process an entire code repository or long-form legal document, a major upgrade for regulated and technical workflows. Sources [KuCoin News: GLM-5.2 Launch Details↗](https://kucoin.com/news/flash/zhipu-ai-launches-glm-5-2-with-1m-context-support-api-and-open-source-release-scheduled-for-next-week "Open source: https://kucoin.com/news/flash/zhipu-ai-launches-glm-5-2-with-1m-cont...

Open Source AI.content: [CoddyKit](/) [0](/subscription/subscription)[Pricing](/subscription/subscription) # FreeLLMAPI: The Open-Source Tool With 22,400+ GitHub Stars That Gives You 7.4 Billion Free AI Tokens Every Month FreeLLMAPI is an open-source tool with 22,400+ GitHub stars that aggregates 34 free LLM providers behind a single OpenAI-compatible API endpoint, delivering 7.4 billion free tokens per month with smart routing, automatic failover, and encrypted key storage. C CoddyKit Team · 9 min read · 1,824 words ![FreeLLMAPI: The Open-Source Tool With 22,400+ GitHub Stars That Gives You 7.4 Billion Free AI Tokens Every Month](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1558494949-ef010cbdcc31?w=1200&h=630&fit=crop) **Quick Answer:** FreeLLMAPI is an open-source TypeScript tool that aggregates free tiers from 34 LLM providers (Google, Groq, Mistral, Cohere, NVIDIA, and more) behind a single OpenAI-compatible API endpoint. It delivers 7.4 billion free tokens per month with smart routing, automatic failover, and encrypted key storage. With 22,400+ GitHub stars, it has become the go-to solution for developers who want powerful AI capabilities without paying for API subscriptions. Every major AI lab now offers a free tier — a few million tokens here, a few thousand requests there. Individually, each tier is limited. But stacked together across 34 providers, they represent roughly **7.4 billion tokens per month** of real inference capacity. The problem? Managing 34 different SDKs, 34 different rate limits, and 34 places a request can fail is a nightmare. That's exactly what [FreeLLMAPI](https://github.com/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi) solves — and why it has exploded to over 22,400 GitHub stars in just four months. If you're a developer learning to build AI-powered applications, or if you simply want to experiment with large language models without burning through your credit card, FreeLLMAPI might be the most important tool you set up this year. ## What Is FreeLLMAPI and Why Does It Matter? FreeLLMAPI is an open-source, self-hosted API gateway that collects free-tier API keys from dozens of AI providers and exposes them through a single OpenAI-compatible `/v1` endpoint. You point any OpenAI SDK client at your local server, and FreeLLMAPI's intelligent router handles the rest — choosing the best available model, falling over to the next provider when one hits a rate limit, and tracking per-key usage so you stay under every free-tier cap. Think of it as a **unified AI gateway** that turns dozens of limited free plans into one robust, high-availability inference API — running entirely on your machine. Here's what makes it special: * **34 free providers** including Google, Groq, Cerebras, Mistral, OpenRouter, Cloudflare, Cohere, NVIDIA, HuggingFace, and 22 more * **635 free model endpoints** spanning 474 model families * **Full OpenAI API compatibility** — chat completions, embeddings, image generation, audio, video, and more * **Smart routing with 6 strategies** — speed, capability, and reliability scoring * **AES-256-GCM encrypted key storage** — your provider keys never leave your machine unencrypted * **Self-updating model catalog** — new free models appear automatically ## How FreeLLMAPI Works Under the Hood FreeLLMAPI is built in TypeScript and runs as a lightweight Node.js server (~40 MB RSS at idle). Here's the architecture in simple terms: ### 1. Key Management You add your free-tier API keys through a clean React dashboard. Each key is encrypted with AES-256-GCM and stored in a local SQLite database. Your applications only ever interact with a single unified `freellmapi-...` bearer token — they never see your provider keys directly. ### 2. Smart Routing Engine When a request arrives, the router evaluates your provider chain based on live per-model scores for speed, capability, and reliability. It selects the best available model, checks per-key rate counters (RPM, RPD, TPM, TPD), and dispatches the request. If a provider returns a 429 (rate limit) or 5xx err...

This preconfigured AMI on AWS delivers a fully operational Flowise environment, eliminating manual installation and configuration so teams can start building agentic applications immediately after launch. Open-source platform, with over 3k stars on GitHub. ## [​](#quick-start) Quick Start The fastest way to set up your agent with LangWatch and get started is by using LangWatch Skills via a coding assistant. Open Source AI.content: [Ready-made creative pipelines](/workflows)[Use cases Ways to use Morphic](/usecases)[Case studies Workflows in action](/casestudy)[Creative Offerings Strategic guidance for teams](/creative-offerings)[Creator Fund Fueling original stories](/creator-fund) [News and product updates](/blog)[Our philosophy](/manifesto)[Meet the team](/about)[Assets and guidelines](/brand) What's new [Seedance 2.5 on Morphic 30-second single takes, native audio, and up to 50 reference inputs.](/resources/models/seedance-2-5) # The 8 best open source AI video models in 2026 Compare the 8 best open source AI video models in 2026 for teams that want weights they can download, self-host, and fine-tune. The right pick depends on output quality, license terms, and the GPU you have to run it on. Morphic is not open source, but it is the fastest way to run open models like Wan and LTX, plus flagship closed ones, with no GPU setup. [Try now](https://studio.morphic.com/tools/text-to-video/run?utm_campaign=resources_tools&utm_content=best-open-source-ai-video-models_hero&utm_term=en) ## Open source AI video models at a glance Each model below leads on something specific: raw quality, motion, speed on modest hardware, license permissiveness, or ecosystem support. The table is sorted by what each one delivers best, so you can match the model to your setup and license needs instead of picking by ranking alone. | Tool | Best for | Standout feature | | --- | --- | --- | | 1.Morphic | Running open and closed video models without hardware | Open and flagship closed models on one Canvas | | 2.Wan (Alibaba) | Best overall open weights quality | Strong quality with a permissive license | | 3.LTX Video (Lightricks) | Fast generation on consumer GPUs | Near real-time speed on modest hardware | | 4.HunyuanVideo (Tencent) | Cinematic quality from open weights | Large model with strong prompt adherence | | 5.Mochi 1 (Genmo) | Fluid motion under a permissive license | High-fidelity motion, Apache licensed | | 6.CogVideoX (Zhipu / THUDM) | An accessible starting point for self-hosting | Multiple sizes for modest hardware | | 7.Stable Video Diffusion (Stability AI) | Basic image-to-video with broad support | Deep integration across open tooling | | 8.Open-Sora (HPC-AI Tech) | Full transparency and research use | Open weights, training pipeline, and recipe | [Try Morphic](https://studio.morphic.com/tools/text-to-video/run?utm_campaign=resources_tools&utm_content=best-open-source-ai-video-models_inline&utm_term=en) ## The 8 best open source AI video models for every use case ### Morphic Run open models like Wan and LTX, plus flagship closed ones like Veo and Kling, in one visual Canvas with no GPU setup. * Open source video models are powerful, but running them means a capable GPU, CUDA drivers, a ComfyUI or diffusers setup, and time. Morphic hosts open models like Wan and LTX so you can generate from a prompt without any of that. * The same workspace runs the flagship closed models too, Veo, Kling, Seedance, Hailuo, and Vidu, so you can compare an open model against a closed one on the exact same shot before you commit. * Clips land on a free-flowing visual Canvas and stay live. Line the selects up on Compose, the built-in timeline, add generated voiceover and music, and export the finished cut without leaving the workspace. * To be clear: Morphic is a hosted platform, not an open source project. If your requirement is downloading weights to self-host or fine-tune, run the open models directly. If your requirement is generating with them fast, this removes the setup. According to TechCrunch, the next layer of competition is moving into the systems around the chip — how data moves, how compute is orchestrated, how storage and networking perform, and how massive AI data centers operate efficiently at scale. That matters. For years, Nvidia’s story was simple: AI needs GPUs. Nvidia makes the best GPUs. Demand explodes. But as hyperscalers and chipmakers build alternatives, the bigger question is not just who has the best processor. It is who can make the entire AI factory work better. The future of AI infrastructure is becoming less about one component and more about the full system: Compute. Memory. Networking. Storage. Energy efficiency. Data movement. Orchestration. Performance per watt. That is the real lesson for businesses too. AI success does not come from buying one tool. It comes from making the whole system work together. The companies that win with AI will not just adopt powerful technology. They will build the infrastructure, workflows, and operating discipline to use it well. That creates a wider set of potential winners, and also fresh risks if expectations run ahead of reality. This article walks through three stocks from a Global AI Infrastructure Enablers screener that appear positively exposed to this trend. It is designed to help you decide whether they deserve a closer look or a spot on your watchlist. The three stocks below are only a starting sample. The full screen surfaced 56 more large, AI-infrastructure-linked companies with equally compelling narratives that are not covered in this article. To identify and analyze the highest conviction ideas that fit your own criteria, head straight into the [Global AI Infrastructure Enablers (Semiconductors, Cloud & Networking) screener](https://simplywall.st/screener/create). The business is highly focused, with all reported revenue of about US$756 million coming from semiconductors, and it serves memory makers, chip designers and hyperscalers across the United States, South Korea, Singapore and other regions. The stock has a market cap of roughly US$9.3b, putting it firmly in the large cap camp within AI hardware and cloud infrastructure. Rambus may appeal to investors who want exposure to the plumbing of AI rather than only the headline GPU suppliers. Its DDR5 server chipsets and high speed memory and security IP are already tied to AI data center buildouts. Recent earnings reports and product launches illustrate how deeper AI workloads can translate into richer chip content per server. At the same time, heavy reliance on a few memory product lines, margin pressure and insider selling mean expectations matter, and execution on new technologies such as MRDIMM and companion chips will be important to watch. The full story around AI driven demand, revenue concentration and valuation expectations is a key consideration for long term investors. Rambus is already wired into AI data center buildouts, yet many investors focus only on headline GPUs. Infra & Chips.content: ## Unbox Factory's Post --- ### [**Unbox Factory**](https://www.facebook.com/unboxfactory?__cft__[0]=AZYGygHGxt0VF61fNNdeu3lDIswD_YLzp623WEJOfzeveoN0lAzJnOSbfK5dJjQ-egwsiHazsiVojC2pd2Pk8uKi5ebbxOFa0Ug7UPwAAQbnRZ6olNzaQRbZoYyp72wjdpNG-zHqJd58VakzsNFMCpJ8FlQNacEK4lu0A5mJmlMCDw&__tn__=-UC%2CP-R) [1h](https://www.facebook.com/unboxfactory/posts/pfbid0UN722yDf55H1DJ3hbL79CSqyqkPZWUjFmWHhYXoQQorxmiigB57MWKaWk3b7d5Lkl?__cft__[0]=AZYGygHGxt0VF61fNNdeu3lDIswD_YLzp623WEJOfzeveoN0lAzJnOSbfK5dJjQ-egwsiHazsiVojC2pd2Pk8uKi5ebbxOFa0Ug7UPwAAQbnRZ6olNzaQRbZoYyp72wjdpNG-zHqJd58VakzsNFMCpJ8FlQNacEK4lu0A5mJmlMCDw&__tn__=%2CO%2CP-R)  · NVIDIA generated a record $96.2 billion in quarterly revenue for the quarter ended July 26, 2026—an extraordinary 106% increase from the same quarter a year earlier and 18% higher than the previous quarter. The biggest driver was its Data Center business, which generated approximately $89 billion, up 117% year over year. NVIDIA also reported approximately $59.7 billion in quarterly profit, showing just how enormous the AI infrastructure boom has become. NVIDIA expects another record quarter, forecasting approximately $108 billion in revenue—meaning the company could soon be generating more than $100 billion every three months. The numbers demonstrate that the AI boom is no longer a small technology cycle. It is creating enormous demand for GPUs, networking equipment, data centers, electricity and advanced cooling infrastructure. Source: NVIDIA, August 27, 2026 Infra & Chips.content: [Accessibility Menu](#) [▲ S&P 500 **+---%**|▲ Stock Advisor **+---%**Join The Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/mms/mark/e-foolcom-sa-top-nav-returns) [Accessibility](#)[Help](https://support.fool.com/) [![The Motley Fool](https://g.foolcdn.com/misc-assets/logo-tmf-primary-1-magenta-purple-reversed.svg?_w=320)![The Motley Fool](https://g.foolcdn.com/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fg.foolcdn.com%2Fmisc-assets%2Ftmf_holdingco_logo_stacked_magenta_royalpurple_rev.png&w=96&op=resize)](/) **Broadcom** ([AVGO](/quote/nasdaq/avgo/) -0.74%) and **Advanced Micro Devices** ([AMD](/quote/nasdaq/amd/) -2.33%) sit side by side in many [artificial intelligence (AI)](https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/market-sectors/information-technology/ai-stocks/) hardware conversations, yet the market makes it clear they are not the same kind of stock. Broadcom looks like a [cash-rich infrastructure utility](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/10/broadcom-stock-looks-like-a-screaming-deal/). AMD looks more like a leveraged bet on a shift in which players will supply the brains of data centers. That difference, more than any single metric, is what their valuations are signaling. ![Letters A and I fall in a hurricane.](https://g.foolcdn.com/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fg.foolcdn.com%2Feditorial%2Fimages%2F883329%2Fgettyimages-2155811445.jpg&w=3840&op=resize) Image source: Getty Images. ## Broadcom: Contracted AI infrastructure [Broadcom's](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/27/should-you-buy-broadcom-stock-while-its-under-400/) AI business is built around selling high-speed networking equipment and designing custom accelerators for hyperscalers that want their own bespoke silicon. It [co-designs application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs)](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/06/02/asic-demand-broadcom-no-brainer-buy/) for customers such as **Microsoft**, **Alphabet**, **Amazon**, and **Meta Platforms**. Each of these chips is narrowly built for the specific model mix and power envelope of the buyer, in contrast to the general-purpose GPUs sold by AMD, **Nvidia** ([NVDA](/quote/nasdaq/nvda/) -4.58%), and others. Because of this, ASICs can be more efficient and less costly to use than GPUs for the precise types of workloads they are designed for. Those ASIC programs are large. Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue sits near $8.4 billion per quarter, with a disclosed AI chip backlog of around $73 billion, and management is now talking about a line of sight to more than $100 billion in AI revenue in 2027. Custom ASIC servers are on track to reach about 27.8% of AI server shipments in 2026, with ASIC sales volumes growing 44.6% year over year, well ahead of the growth pace of merchant GPUs. Layer that on top of Broadcom's established businesses in networking, broadband, and enterprise software, and the tech giant starts to look like an AI-enabled toll road. ![Broadcom Stock Quote](https://g.foolcdn.com/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fg.foolcdn.com%2Fart%2Fcompanylogos%2Fmark%2FAVGO.png&w=128&op=resize) ## [NASDAQ: AVGO](/quote/nasdaq/avgo/) Premium Feature Moneyball Superscore 90/100 Today's Change (-0.74%) $-2.75 Current Price $368.79 ### Key Data Points Market Cap $1.8TMarket cap calculated using publicly traded shares outstanding only. Does not include unlisted, private, or dual-class non-traded shares. Implied market cap may vary. Day's Range $365.35- $376.59 52wk Range $287.17- $495.00 Volume 16.6M Avg Vol 26.1M Gross Margin 65.66% Dividend Yield 0.69% ## AMD: Taking aim at Nvidia [AMD](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/25/amd-stock-is-rising-heres-why-this-top-ai-stock-is/) plays a different game. It is not trying to help customers build in-house alternatives to Nvidia's GPUs -- it's trying to *be* the alternative. Its Instinct MI350 and MI355X accelerators and Helios rack designs target Nvidia's B200 GPUs and its new Rubin platform in data center AI. That difference, more than any single metric, is what their valuations are signaling. ![Letters A and I fall in a hurricane.](https://g.foolcdn.com/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fg.foolcdn.com%2Feditorial%2Fimages%2F883329%2Fgettyimages-2155811445.jpg&w=3840&op=resize) Image source: Getty Images. ## Broadcom: Contracted AI infrastructure [Broadcom's](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/27/should-you-buy-broadcom-stock-while-its-under-400/) AI business is built around selling high-speed networking equipment and designing custom accelerators for hyperscalers that want their own bespoke silicon. It [co-designs application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs)](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/06/02/asic-demand-broadcom-no-brainer-buy/) for customers such as **Microsoft**, **Alphabet**, **Amazon**, and **Meta Platforms**. Each of these chips is narrowly built for the specific model mix and power envelope of the buyer, in contrast to the general-purpose GPUs sold by AMD, **Nvidia** ([NVDA](/quote/nasdaq/nvda/) -4.58%), and others. Because of this, ASICs can be more efficient and less costly to use than GPUs for the precise types of workloads they are designed for. Those ASIC programs are large. Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue sits near $8.4 billion per quarter, with a disclosed AI chip backlog of around $73 billion, and management is now talking about a line of sight to more than $100 billion in AI revenue in 2027. Custom ASIC servers are on track to reach about 27.8% of AI server shipments in 2026, with ASIC sales volumes growing 44.6% year over year, well ahead of the growth pace of merchant GPUs. Layer that on top of Broadcom's established businesses in networking, broadband, and enterprise software, and the tech giant starts to look like an AI-enabled toll road. ![Broadcom Stock Quote](https://g.foolcdn.com/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fg.foolcdn.com%2Fart%2Fcompanylogos%2Fmark%2FAVGO.png&w=128&op=resize) ## [NASDAQ: AVGO](/quote/nasdaq/avgo/) Premium Feature Moneyball Superscore 90/100 Today's Change (-0.74%) $-2.75 Current Price $368.79 ### Key Data Points Market Cap $1.8TMarket cap calculated using publicly traded shares outstanding only. Infra & Chips.content: [Get Started](/sign-up) ![Nvidia earnings 2026,NVDA stock analysis,AI chip market,Nvidia Q2 results,Nvidia revenue growth](https://prod-intellectia-open-documents.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/user-GT8TSM04NZMggRmDNxWD/82f6d5bce0dd57b31c8ac43eaa771f2c21506405ece0528090d4bffe74acb76a.WEBP) # Nvidia Q2 Earnings 2026: Record $96.2B Revenue and the Future of AI Chips 2026-08-309mins ![Jason Huang](https://prod-intellectia-open-documents.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/user-Xx60D4Y8Y25WmPdNX4rt/74645b2239ec075ecb954b760ba523de7e3aefd2671f70e8648df8732dedb958.png) Written byJason Huang Content ## Key Takeaway Nvidia has once again shattered expectations with its fiscal second-quarter earnings for 2026, reporting a staggering $96.22 billion in revenue—a remarkable 106% year-over-year increase that cements the company's position as the undisputed leader in artificial intelligence infrastructure. The AI chip giant delivered adjusted earnings per share of $2.22, comfortably beating Wall Street's consensus estimate of $2.10 and demonstrating the sustained explosive demand for its data center accelerators. The results validate Nvidia's strategic positioning at the center of the AI revolution, with data center revenue reaching approximately $89 billion for the quarter. This performance comes as hyperscale customers like Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Meta continue to invest billions in AI infrastructure to power their cloud services and large language models. The company's Blackwell architecture GPUs, which began ramping in volume during the quarter, are commanding premium pricing and contributing significantly to margin expansion. For investors, Nvidia's Q2 results provide compelling evidence that the AI infrastructure buildout remains in its early innings. With an estimated 80-85% market share in AI data center accelerators, Nvidia has built a formidable moat that competitors are struggling to breach. However, potential headwinds including semiconductor tariffs, increasing competition from AMD and custom ASICs, and questions about the sustainability of current growth rates warrant careful consideration as the stock trades at elevated valuations. ## Breaking Down the Numbers: Nvidia's Record Quarter Nvidia's fiscal Q2 2027 results, reported on August 26, 2026, represent one of the most impressive financial performances in corporate history. The company's total revenue of $96.22 billion represents a 106% increase from the $46.7 billion reported in the same quarter last year, demonstrating that demand for AI computing power continues to accelerate rather than normalize. The adjusted earnings per share of $2.22 represents a significant beat against analyst expectations of $2.10, with gross margins expanding as the company's product mix shifts toward higher-value AI accelerators. Data center revenue, which now accounts for the vast majority of Nvidia's business, reached approximately $89 billion—up from roughly $42 billion in the year-ago quarter. Within this segment, hyperscale revenues grew 102% year-over-year to $48.71 billion, while AI Cloud and Enterprise revenues surged 138% to $40.31 billion. These numbers become even more impressive when viewed in historical context. Nvidia's data center revenue has grown from under $3 billion in fiscal 2020 to approximately $93.7 billion in fiscal 2026—a remarkable 65-fold increase in just six years. This transformation reflects the company's successful pivot from a gaming-focused GPU manufacturer to the essential infrastructure provider for the AI era. ## The Blackwell Effect: Next-Generation AI Chips Drive Growth A significant portion of Nvidia's Q2 strength came from the ramp-up of its Blackwell architecture GPUs, the company's latest generation of AI accelerators that began shipping in volume during the quarter. These chips represent a substantial leap forward in performance and efficiency, enabling customers to train larger AI models and run more complex inference workloads at lower total cost of owners...
